findings.note: "Most owners in this spot wait too long, and you will usually pay more the longer you wait, so you should never delay." States a frequency about owners, a cost outcome and an absolute instruction. No ledger claim supports any of it. It also contradicts the brief (no costs, no outcome promise) and the section's own point that some families reasonably choose not to clear first. Remove the sentence or replace it with a conditional line that states no fact, for example that waiting has its own costs and the seller should weigh time against cost with their professionals.

"It does not remove your duty to tell the buyer what you know." is a flat legal duty with a scope ("what you know") that neither clm:6 nor clm:7 states. Ledger only supports: the article applies to a transfer by sale of single-family residential property except as provided in 1102.2 (clm:6), and any waiver of its requirements is void (clm:7). Reword to stay within those claims, for example that a cleanout does not change the disclosure requirements that apply to a sale of single-family residential property, which cannot be waived, with the exception in 1102.2 noted.

The unit makes disclosure-duty language with no confirm-with-a-professional wording anywhere in it. Add a short line telling the seller to confirm what must be disclosed on the Transfer Disclosure Statement with a real estate attorney or their listing agent.

required_actions: Remove or rewrite the 'Most owners ... never delay' paragraph so it states no frequency, cost or outcome.
Reword 'duty to tell the buyer what you know' to match clm:6 and clm:7 (single-family residential, exception in 1102.2, waiver void).
Add confirm-with-attorney/listing-agent language for disclosure questions.
